summary: Tenant migration between Dedicated pools causes delayed pin reconciliation, silent fallback to safe-variant and token spike
description:
Issue summary: During an automated tenant migration from one Dedicated GPU pool to another in us-east-1, several customer sessions experienced a delayed model-version pin reconciliation. As a consequence the routing layer silently diverted a subset of traffic to the safe fallback variant (rwd-pegasus-13b-v2->rwd-pegasus-13b-quant) for ~18 minutes, which produced higher token counts and a billing spike for the customer.

Impact: NimbleHealth reported a 2.6x increase in token consumption for ~27% of their active sessions during the window. Customer-facing latency remained within SLOs but model outputs changed (quantized variant had higher repetition on longer prompts). Customer flagged potential data-quality regression and unexpected invoice increase.

Environment: Production Dedicated pool migration (us-east-1). Migration triggered via Reserved Capacity reassignment job: rc-migrate-2026-03-12-08. Canary group size: 5% traffic.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Start RC reassignment job with canary slice enabled and pin-preserve=true. 2) Observe orchestrator snapshot push to new pool controllers. 3) During controller handoff, trigger tenant session reconnects (customer used connection drain time of 30s). 4) Watch pin reconciliation logs and edge routing decisions.

Observed behavior: - Orchestrator commit acknowledged on new pool, but tenant pin state in edge-cache showed stale affinity for ~18 minutes. - Edge routing fallback policy moved sessions to quantized safe-variant under conservative health probe conditions. - KV cache entries for tenant affinity had TTL refresh suppressed due to an optimization that batches repinning writes during pool operations. - Billing meter reported token counts attributed to quantized variant for impacted requests; customer invoice shows unexpected delta.

Expected behavior: Tenant pin should be preserved across pool migrations when pin-preserve=true or, if temporarily unpinned, orchestrator and edge should annotate traffic to make fallback transparent to billing and downstream quality checks.

Initial hypothesis: A write-batching optimization in the orchestrator's pin reconciler deferred the final pin commit until snapshot stabilization. Edge cache read path fell back to safe-variant when it detected missing/expired pin. The batching delay overlapped with tenant reconnect activity causing partial cohort to be routed to fallback variant.

investigation: Logs reviewed: orchestrator-controller.log (08:10-08:40), edge-cache.log (08:12-08:40), billing-metrics for tenant (08:00-09:00).

Found a replicated sequence: orchestrator snapshot v87 -> v88 -> v89; the reconciler delayed final commit until v89 stabilization. During this window, edge cache had an expired affinity entry which triggered fallback routing policy.

Pin reconciler code path: discovered two contributing conditions: (1) max_batch_delay defaulted to 15s but under retry storms could be extended due to exponential backoff bug, (2) a boolean flag 'suppress_edge_refresh' was set during pool reassign path and wasn't cleared on some error paths.

Traffic analysis: 27% of active sessions for nimble-tenant-42 were re-established during the commit window (customer's client uses aggressive reconnect on socket drop). Those sessions show routing to quantized variant based on fallback logs.
Billing telemetry: token attribution logic labeled requests by variant_id returned by serving runtime; because variant changed midstream, tokens were recorded under quantized SKU.
resolution: Short-term mitigation (2026-03-14 08:40): Forced orchestrator.pin_reconciler.max_batch_delay=0 for us-east-1 migrations and cleared suppress_edge_refresh flag via orchestration tool. Edge cache warmup handshake deployed to force immediate affinity refresh post-commit.

Customer communication: Notified NimbleHealth of the mitigation steps and offered to open a billing review. Finance will review the token delta for the window and propose a credit if appropriate. (Point of contact: Sarah Chen)

Code fix: Eng PR #1482 removes suppression on edge refresh and adds stronger error-path clearing for suppress_edge_refresh. It also removes exponential backoff extension on pin commit delay during migrations. PR pending review and targeted for fast-track backport to the 2026-03-15 hotfix release.

Follow-ups: 1) Add an orchestrator-edge contract test to verify pin visibility within 5s after commit during pool operations. 2) Update runbook to disable batching optimization for dedicated pool reassignments unless explicitly allowed. 3) Perform retrospective to identify other customers affected during same migration window (job rc-migrate-2026-03-12-08).
Status: Mitigations applied and monitoring; awaiting PR merge and customer billing resolution.
